title: Anchored Trace Responder for VPC Edge Debugging
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated / Private deployments report that when calls traverse the VPC edge collector -> perimeter relay -> central ingest, span parentage is frequently lost and debugging production issues requires correlation by request-id + time window. This is especially painful for private clusters where we cannot ship full traces and must rely on edge-local artifacts.

Goal: Implement an 'Anchored Trace Responder' component in the VPC/On‑prem collector that: (1) preserves and translates trace context across boundary hops without leaking tenant identifiers, (2) emits a concise replayable digest (anchored trace 'token') that allows later server-side rehydration and lookup, and (3) offers a debug endpoint to pull expanded trace fragments for support/incident workflows.

Scope: edge collector agent + perimeter relay shim + console debug UI hook. This ticket implements the agent + relay changes and produces the runbook and telemetry to integrate with the console feature (console UI work tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Anchor token created when a trace crosses the VPC edge and surface token in telemetry headers (X-RW-ANCHOR) without embedding tenant id or PII.
Server-side rehydration service can accept anchor token and return a 5s window of spans matching the anchored KV hash (test harness for local replay).
No cross-tenant trace data is present in the anchor token (automated test for tenant isolation).
Edge collector falls back to local spool and re-emits anchored digests on network restore, preserving ordering and rate limits.
Latency overhead at the edge < 2ms per request p50 for anchor generation under typical load (benchmarked).
Security review completed with KMS integration plan for signing tokens and redaction checklist approved.
implementation_notes: Anchor token = SHA256(span-root-id || tenant-opaque-hash || short-window-millis) signed with local KMS key; store ephemeral mapping in edge spool (TTL 24h).
Do not include tenant id or span content in the token. Use tenant-opaque-hash derived from tenant key material so token cannot be brute-forced across tenants.
Add a config toggle 'tracing.anchor.enabled' defaulted to true for Private/Dedicated until rollout finishes.
Perimeter relay will implement token whitelist and mapping probe to validate signature and TTL before contacting central rehydration endpoint.
Bench harness: use local vBench with mixed seq lengths and simulate 50k rps across 4 edge instances to measure overhead and spool behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag enable for internal dogfood private clusters. 2) Collect benchmark metrics and SLO telemetry for 2 weeks. 3) Enable in customer beta for 2 enterprise accounts behind a toggle. 4) Gradually enable for all Dedicated deployments after monitoring. Any rollouts will include a fallback that strips anchors (no failure on invalid token).
qa_plan: Unit tests for token generation and signature verification.
Integration test: end-to-end trace anchored token generation -> central rehydration mock -> span retrieval validation.
Fuzz tests to ensure no tenant id or raw span data is encoded into token under aggressive sampling.
Chaos test: simulate network outage, validate spool replay and duplicate suppression.
